solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brats go up to vandalise superior hostelry

definitions.note: a pub that serves upmarket food

indicators.note: to vandalise is to wreck, so the letters of these three words are smashed up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Unruly youths head off to smash up a smart pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a public house raised above the ordinary by serving restaurant-quality meals.

clue.text: Mollusc that has one looking amazed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large clam whose shell gapes open
second meaning: someone who stares open-mouthed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the idea of a shellfish looking astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is both a burrowing clam with a permanently open shell and a person who stares in wonder.

clue.text: Chief has drink with engineers

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: The boss shares a drink with the engineering crew.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank, the same as principal or foremost.

clue.text: Moves made by members of the family holding firm after upset

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the family surrounds the firm

parts.note: relations are relatives, family members

indicators.note: after upset means the firm's letters are turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Relatives with a company stake make moves after a family upset.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the firm's letters upside down, so they read bottom to top inside the family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Relocations are moves to a new place, plural noun for plural noun.

clue.text: Characters that could be hard up in social isolation

indicators.note: could be means these letters might form a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone broke is cut off from society.
explanation.walkthrough: Purdah is the practice in some Muslim and Hindu societies of secluding women from public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah has the extended sense of seclusion, being kept away from public life.

clue.text: Second-rate monarch is moving

definitions.note: a verb phrase; betaking oneself means going, so the participle matches 'moving' while the 'is' is absorbed

parts.note: beta is a grade below alpha, second-rate
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A lesser king is on his way.
explanation.walkthrough: To betake oneself is an old way of saying to go somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Betaking, as in betaking oneself, means going or travelling somewhere.

clue.text: Important person with a billion banked?

definitions.text: Important person with a billion banked?

indicators.note: banked means deposited, here placed inside the person as if in a vault

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or upper-class person, a bigwig

explanation.surface: A rich big shot with a billion stashed in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as both wordplay and definition: a nabob is just the sort of grandee who would have a billion salted away.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob, originally a Mughal governor, came to mean a person of great wealth and status.

clue.text: Bright light upsets these Greek characters

indicators.note: upsets means turns upside down, which in a down clue reverses the letters

parts.note: the sun is a bright light

explanation.surface: A dazzling glare makes Greek letters hard to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, so the plural is these letters.

clue.text: In quarrel notice piercing tool

indicators.note: In means the notice goes inside the quarrel

parts.note: a brawl is a noisy quarrel
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A noticeboard row turns nasty when a sharp tool comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small hand tool for making holes in wood before a screw goes in.

clue.text: Bishop has deficiency, predicament from which there's no getting away

definitions.text: from which there's no getting away
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the thing nothing can escape

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
lack means a shortage
being in a hole is being in a predicament

explanation.surface: A cleric short of money finds himself in a fix he cannot escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits after 'predicament', which reads as though it heads the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A black hole is a region of space whose gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.

clue.text: In part of East End that's housing for the toffs?

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the district holds the toffs' letter within it

parts.note: Poplar is a district of London's East End
U stands for upper class, the toffs

explanation.surface: Is there an area of working-class London where posh folk set up home?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' at the start looks like a link word but it is the definition, as in 'flares are in'. Poplar is a district of East London; U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is 'in' is fashionable, the same as being widely liked.

clue.text: Bit of food? Child eats seconds with a mother going short

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the child surrounds the letter

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: going short means losing its final letter, so the mother is cut by one

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A child gobbles second helpings while mum skimps on her own share.
explanation.walkthrough: DAM (an animal's mother) loses its last letter to give DA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a Mexican fried tortilla, a snack or item of food.

clue.text: River for you to sit beside somewhere in Sussex

indicators.note: to sit beside means the second piece is placed next to the first

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A riverside spot where you might sit somewhere in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is a small historic town in East Sussex, in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a town in East Sussex, so it is a location in that county.

clue.text: One takes the biscuit, as against a donkey?

definitions.note: a crackerjack is an excellent one, a person or thing that stands out

indicators.note: as against means placed next to, set up against the first piece

parts.note: a cracker is a crisp savoury biscuit
a jack is a male donkey, a jackass

explanation.surface: Someone grabs the biscuit rather than feeding it to the donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the' links definition and wordplay, and nods to the British idiom 'takes the biscuit', meaning to be the most remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackerjack means an excellent person or thing, someone first-rate.

clue.text: Like message passed on to be perused, having got tidied up?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: a message forwarded is readdressed

parts.note: read is the past participle of read, perused
dressed means tidied up, as in dressed ranks or a dressed shop window

explanation.surface: A forwarded note is read once it has been neatened.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter sent on to a new location has been readdressed, its envelope given a fresh destination.

clue.text: About to dive into water? Hold it!

indicators.note: to dive into means the first piece plunges inside the second

parts.note: a bath is a tub of water
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A swimmer about to plunge in is told to take a gulp of air first.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a command, but 'it' is what you hold before going under.
explanation.definitionFit: One holds one's breath, the air in the lungs, before going underwater.

clue.text: Bit of wood left at back of farm in risky operation

indicators.note: in means the farm and the letter sit inside the risky venture

parts.note: a bet is a risky venture

indicators.note: at back of means this letter goes at the end of the farm

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm

explanation.surface: A twig left behind the farm during a dangerous job.
explanation.definitionFit: A branchlet is a small branch, a twig on a tree.

clue.text: Giant oil spills making a sort of design

indicators.note: spills suggests the letters slop out and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A huge oil spill leaves a striking pattern on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Intaglio is a design engraved or incised into a surface, the opposite of a relief.

clue.text: Small balls in position one doesn't want to lose

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ball ..., the small metal balls in a bearing

definitions.text: position one doesn't want to lose
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one's ..., one's sense of where one is

explanation.walkthrough: Losing one's bearings means becoming disoriented.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearings are both the metal balls that reduce friction in machinery and one's orientation or location.

clue.text: One grand splashed out for something to make man a man?

definitions.text: something to make man a man?

indicators.note: splashed out suggests spending wildly, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spent a thousand pounds on a product promising to boost manliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splashed out' reads as extravagant spending of the grand.
explanation.definitionFit: An androgen is a male sex hormone such as testosterone, which produces masculine characteristics.

clue.text: Relaxation of French taking wine with English

parts.note: de is French for of
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman unwinds with a glass alongside an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine, used in Communion.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is an easing of tension between states, a relaxation of strained relations.

clue.text: Religious proviso one gets in a church offering words of wisdom?

indicators.note: gets in means the proviso and one go inside the other letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
DV is Deo volente, 'God willing', a pious condition attached to plans
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A churchgoer offers wise counsel hedged with 'God willing'.
explanation.walkthrough: DV stands for Deo volente, Latin for 'God willing'; with I it sits between A and CE (Church of England).
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is guidance or counsel, the kind of thing a wise person offers.

clue.text: This writer's needing to demonstrate progress

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I; this writer's means I am, I'm
to prove is to demonstrate

explanation.surface: An author feels the need to show advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to get better, to make headway or advance.

clue.text: City circles infiltrated by the Left

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the circles have the left side slipped inside them

parts.note: O is a circle, so two circles give OO
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A city's political circles have been taken over by left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Left' reads as politics but is the nautical port side.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, Portugal's second city.

clue.text: Tom maybe has a fit of temper — explosive meltdown?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a strop is a sulky fit of bad temper
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: The family cat throws a tantrum and goes completely to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Strop is British slang for a bad mood; HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive, so 'explosive' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a sudden disaster, a total collapse of the kind called a meltdown.

clue.text: Bird, one sadly missing out — it can't fly!

indicators.note: sadly says the word one is jumbled, and missing out says the result is left out of the bird

parts.note: a pigeon is a bird
the letters of one, shuffled into EON by 'sadly'

explanation.surface: A grounded bird mourns its lost companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' scrambles ONE into EON, which 'missing out' removes from PIGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'pigs might fly' rests on the fact that this farm animal cannot take to the air.

clue.text: Visitor with touch of embarrassment breaking wind

indicators.note: breaking means the letter bursts into the middle of the wind

parts.note: a gust is a blast of wind

indicators.note: a touch of something is a tiny amount, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of embarrassment

explanation.surface: A visitor is mortified after passing wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone who visits or stays at another's home.

clue.text: American players — see them briefly in undergarments?

indicators.note: in means the shortened them is placed inside the underwear

parts.note: linen is old-fashioned for underclothes, as in 'dirty linen'
'em is a shortened them

explanation.surface: Footballers glimpsed in their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the inserting. Linemen are American football players on the line of scrimmage.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football, linemen are the players positioned at the line of scrimmage.

clue.text: Crazy girl I dumped

indicators.note: dumped means the letter is thrown away from the girl

parts.note: a maid is a girl

explanation.surface: A man goes wild after his girlfriend ditches him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad means insane or wildly irrational.

clue.text: Gentleman sent back fish dish (it's "crumby")

indicators.note: sent back means the title is turned round, as a dish might be returned to a kitchen

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a gentleman
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A diner returns a fish course for being too crumbly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside hints that a rissole is coated in breadcrumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs, a savoury course.

clue.text: Ultimately that unwanted plant is a border flower

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of that
a weed is a plant growing where it is not wanted

explanation.surface: A gardener says an unwelcome plant is actually a bloom fit for the herbaceous border.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows; the Tweed is the river along the Scottish-English border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river forming part of the boundary between Scotland and England, a flowing stream.

clue.text: Quiet and strange — that is street most badly built?

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
odd means strange
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A hushed, eerie street lined with jerry-built houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy means poorly made, so its superlative describes the worst constructed.
